mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but the mean rank IC over triggered periods is below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5.5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which compresses wage growth and increases input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a statistically significant decline in earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger is not followed by a decline in reported corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) contraction of more than 0.5% from the previous month, combined with a concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10%, signals a broad-based supply shock that raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month -0.5% AND HOUST < previous month -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the joint trigger is not followed by a statistically significant rise in producer price index (PPI) within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 250k for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which precedes a policy response and profit margin compression, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +250k for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger is not followed by a decline in S&P 500 earnings yield within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a coordinated weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the joint decline is not followed by a decline in consumer confidence within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held near zero for more than 12 months in a low-inflation environment signals prolonged monetary accommodation, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS = 0% for >12 months AND CPIAUCSL < 2% annualized
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the trigger is not followed by a statistically significant rise in equity valuations (P/E ratio).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of at least 0.5% and 10%, respectively, alongside a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of at least 0.3 percentage points, signals a broad-based economic contraction that drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month -0.5% AND HOUST < previous month -10% AND UNRATE > previous month +0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the triple-trigger is not followed by a decline in GDP growth within the next quarter.
